sections.h2: 1. Check the Black Friday sale section first
parts: When we checked, ChicChoi's site ran a "Black Friday Sale Now!" banner and a sale section its menu labels "Black Friday 50% Off", with small items such as a Sugar Cube Mini Stapler at $7.20, a School Series loose-leaf notebook at $4.95 and journaling tweezers at $2.90. Add sale items and full-price items to the cart, then try {code} and keep whichever total is lower.

sections.h2: 2. Pick the cheaper color or size
parts: Some ChicChoi products price their versions differently. The Cream Star backpack in Sky Blue was $1.00 less than the other colors, and the Life is Colorful notebook costs $8.20 in A5 and $9.90 in B5. If the color or size doesn't matter to you, the cheaper one plus the code saves the most.

sections.h2: 3. Enter the code before you pay
parts: ChicChoi's refund policy says it can't add a discount code after an order is placed, and that cancelling items costs it a 3% to 4.4% card or PayPal fee. So put everything in one cart, enter {code} at checkout and check the total before you pay.

All orders ship from China to more than 60 countries. ChicChoi says it packs orders in 1 to 4 business days, then delivery takes 8 to 14 business days to the US, 6 to 8 to Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Singapore, and 6 to 10 to the UK and most of the EU. Every parcel is tracked. Shipping is priced by weight and destination at checkout, with free-shipping promotions now and then. For US, UK and EU orders, ChicChoi says it pays import duties and VAT, so there's nothing extra to pay on delivery.

For a change of mind, contact ChicChoi within 30 days of delivery. You pay the return postage to China, shipping fees aren't refunded and a 10% restocking fee is taken off. Damaged or faulty items are handled within 30 days of delivery by replacement or another fix. Refunds can go back to your card or PayPal, or as store credit with a 5% bonus. Our [ChicChoi review](saving-tips-chicchoi-review.html) sums up the ratings and the fine print.
